messages:
Mira Chen: quick sync on API Keys UX — focused on rotate / disable / revoke flows. dropping current Figma and copy snippets here. main goals: make intent explicit, avoid accidental destructive actions, and fix a11y keyboard flow. can we review copy + microcopy and list any must-haves for dev?

Olivia Park: sounds good. two high-level asks from design: 1) separate 'Disable' (temporary, reversible) from 'Revoke' (permanent), 2) when showing secrets, make clear it's shown only once. also prefer descriptive button labels instead of Yes/No.

Sam Ortiz: backend notes: both operations supported. `disable` toggles flag, safe to re-enable. `revoke` nukes secret material and emits audit + optional org notification. small constraint: rotation will generate a new secret; we only return it in response once.

Lee Nguyen: frontend findings from prototype: modal focus trap sometimes loses focus to page behind. will implement: on open, focus primary, trap focus, on close return focus to originating kebab/menu button. also modals should use `role=alertdialog` and `aria-describedby` to reference explanatory body copy.

Jamal Price: security checklist: never store plaintext secret after rotate; require explicit user copy / download action. rotation modal should surface a single-use banner: "This secret will not be shown again." Add an audit event on revoke and rotate. Warn if key has wildcard scopes.

Mira Chen: draft modal copy — please nit: 
```
Heading: Disable or Revoke API key
Body: Disabling temporarily prevents new requests using this key. Revoking permanently removes the key and cannot be undone.
Radio: ( ) Disable key — Temporarily stop this key (can be re-enabled)
( ) Revoke key — Permanently remove this key (irreversible, recommended to create replacement)
Primary (Disable): Disable key
Primary (Revoke): Revoke key (danger)
Secondary: Cancel
```
Question: should we keep both actions inside one modal (with radio) or separate modals?

Olivia Park: prefer separate flows to avoid accidental selection. default primary should be 'Disable key' on the main list action (so soft action is one click). If a user selects 'Revoke', open a second confirmation modal with stronger language and visual danger affordance.

Lee Nguyen: separate modals easier for a11y too — simpler focus management and clearer `aria-describedby` for the stronger revoke modal.

Sam Ortiz: agree with separate endpoints. we'll mark `revoke` as irreversible in swagger and include idempotency keys. also plan to emit `org.alerts` if revoked key had admin scopes.

a11y-bot: automated scan: flagged two issues on current comps: 1) danger red text contrast below AA (button label on gray), 2) ambiguous button text ('Confirm'/'Cancel') — screen reader sees no context. recommend labels like `Disable key` / `Cancel` / `Revoke key`.

Mira Chen: empty state copy draft for Keys page: 
"No API keys yet — create a key to start calling the Redwood API. Follow the security guide to scope keys and rotate regularly." CTA: Create API key
Accessibility question: should we include a keyboard shortcut hint for creating keys?

Olivia Park: keyboard shortcut hint ok if it's discoverable; include it in a tooltip rather than empty state copy. keep empty state copy short. add a small link to the 'Key best practices' doc.

Jamal Price: about showing truncated keys in list: show `sk-****-ef12` pattern. add `aria-label="API key ending ef12"` for screen reader clarity. For rotate success, show full secret in modal with a single 'Copy & Close' primary and a 'Download .txt' secondary. Add `rel=noopener` on download link and `aria-label` as well.

Olivia Park: microcopy suggestion for rotate panel banner: "This secret is only shown once. Store it securely now." keep the tone direct and friendly.

Mira Chen: action items I propose: 
- Lee: modal a11y + focus trap fixes (PR today)
- Sam: ensure endpoints include idempotency and swagger notes (tomorrow)
- Olivia: break revoke into separate confirm modal in Figma and update copy (tomorrow morning)
- Jamal: update security checklist and audit triggers (after endpoints ready)

Lee Nguyen: will push the focus/fix PR and add `role=alertdialog` markup and `aria-describedby` IDs.

Sam Ortiz: will add `/disable` and `/revoke` endpoints and docs. plan to include audit event schemas in the swagger PR.

a11y-bot: will re-run checks after PR. will specifically verify contrast and button labels.

Mira Chen: thanks — I'll consolidate final copy here once design changes are in. small copy followup: prefer "prevents any new requests" vs "temporarily stops usage"? I think explicit is better.

Olivia Park: use "prevents any new requests from using this key." explicit and consistent.

Mira Chen: perfect. wrapping up. I'll post the final acceptance criteria and paste the final modal copy in this thread when ready.
